newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq asks U.N. to press Iran on Uday's attackers.
newsitem.headline: Iraq asks U.N. to press Iran on Uday's attackers.

text.p: Iraq has asked the United Nations to put pressure on Iran to either put on trial or hand over the attackers who tried to kill President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday.

Iraqi newspapers on Wednesday carried a letter sent by Iraq's Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf to U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan complaining about the Iranian government's rejection of handing over those who shot and wounded Uday on December 12 while he was driving in Baghdad.
The letter reiterated Baghdad's charges that the attackers belonged to al-Dawa Party (The Call), a Shi'ite Moslem group, who sought refuge in Iran after the attack.

"The letter is in response to Iran's rejection to hand over or put on trial the criminals who committed their crime against the life of Uday Saddam Hussein," said al-Thawra, newspaper of the ruling Baath party.
Uday himself, a few days after the assassination attempt, blamed the attack on Iran, which fought Iraq from 1980 to 1988. Tehran has repeatedly denied the charge.

"Iraq rejects the letter of the Iranian representative (to the U.N.) in New York and urges the U.N. secretary-general to press Iran to try the perpetrators or hand them to the Iraqi authorities," Sahaf said.
In a previous letter to the United Nations, Sahaf accused Iran of sheltering the attackers.

Meantime, director-general of Iraqi Airways Rabee' Mohammad Saleh in press remarks published on Wednesday lambasted Iran for "impeding efforts to know the fate of five Iraqi civilian planes" sent to Tehran to escape U.S. and allied bombings during the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.
Saleh said he had "confirmed information that Iran is using two out of the five planes for demostic flights".
Other Iraqi civil airliners are grounded in Amman and Tunis.
